analysis: Both changed files are test-only (ModelAutopilotUnloadTests.swift adds a WatchdogDuringUnload helper and a watchdogCancelledFinalUnloadFailsAsTransitionStalled test; TransitionWatchdogTests.swift is new). No production code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization, cache-storage or fan-helper paths are modified in the supplied units, so no regression against the threat model (T-041, T-053, T-057, TB-007, TB-011) is identifiable from this evidence. The tests use fixtures with no secrets, temp directories under FileManager temp (removed via defer), loopback ws://127.0.0.1:0 URL, and nil attestationSigner, so there is no new real attack surface. The tests encode security-relevant expectations worth integration attention: stalled autopilot operations must fail closed with transition_stalled rather than succeed after the watchdog fires; stalled preloads are answered but never interrupt in-flight loads; the watchdog neither acts nor reports without consent; shadow/observe-only mode rejects mutation (inactive_session); coordinator unload of unselected models is rejected with model_not_selected; pins follow residency ownership. The production TransitionWatchdog / superviseTransitions implementation and the ProviderLoop test hooks (setStartupPreloadLoadOverrideForTesting, raiseBusyFlagForTesting, etc.) are not in the supplied batch, so the actual enforcement logic, whether those test hooks are compiled out of release builds, and whether the watchdog cancellation could leave a half-applied unload or stranded refusingNewWork state are unverified here and belong to review of the corresponding source files. The tests assert the post-stall state (refusingNewWork false, autopilotCommand nil, stalled command id nil), which is reassuring but not proof of the production behavior.
